Hi Paula — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below.

1) PO line-splitting: Redwood accepts the root PO number and will also record release-level lines. Our default behavior is to echo the customer-supplied PO field back on the invoice and link any release numbers in the invoice metadata. Practically that means your accounting can reconcile to the root PO but still see per-release lines. If you need a strict single-invoice-per-root-PO workflow we can flip a flag in the onboarding Order Form — see attached policy excerpt.

2) MSA redline timing: Kimberly (cc'd) runs legal review for procurement contracts. Typical turnaround for a standard MSA with a few redlines is 3 business days for a first pass; if there are material liability changes it can take longer. Please send the redlines to kimberly_park@redwood.com and she will confirm which proposals require escalation.

Next steps I recommend:
- Paula: send MedSupply's ERP sample (PO + release example) and we will validate mapping.
- Kimberly: will review MedSupply redline and propose a tracked changes doc by Tue EOD.
- Marissa: I asked ops to confirm whether we need an internal onboarding flow update for release-level invoicing.

Logan

Redwood Inference

Paula / Logan — forwarding our initial pass. I took MedSupply's high-level asks (liability cap tweaks, invoice dispute window) and produced a redline. Key decisions:

- Liability cap: we propose keeping the standard Redwood cap but add carveouts for breaches involving third-party data processors; suggested language included.
- Invoice dispute window: we can accept a 60-day dispute window if MedSupply agrees to an invoice validation SLA on their side (sample verification process included).
- PO/invoice mapping: operations confirmed we can support root-PO reconciliation by default; if you want single-invoice enforcement we will add a billing flag in the Order Form and document exceptions.

Please see attached: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx (tracked changes) and an excerpt OrderForm_PO_line-policy.pdf that explains release-level handling.

If MedSupply wants to propose alternate language, please track changes back on the doc and send to this thread. For anything material (indemnity, liability, escrow), we will escalate to senior counsel which will add ~2–4 business days. Otherwise we can typically close in a single review cycle.
